answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted bonding with decaying reputation. New agents enter a shallow lagoon of probation: they bond capital that can only unlock after peers attest useful work over many epochs. A sudden plume of lookalike accounts fails because each clone burns its own bond while earning near-zero attestations. The network then refracts identity through a prism of on-ledger history—attest count, settlement share, and age—so cheap multiplicity cannot outvote long-lived, bonded agents that actually deliver.
